page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor offering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, with 2 threads per core running at 4.2 GHz. Memory allocation stands at 32.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Intel AMX matrix capabilities (AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8), coupled with a 480 MB L3 cache. No local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, requiring external remote block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark analysis reflects consistent middle-tier performance across general compute metrics, highlighted by isolated strengths in compression tasks. The instance produced a PassMark CPU score of 16,760.77 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 9,308.24, placing both within the median 50% band. Read-only cached memory bandwidth reached 689.31 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads and writes achieved 95.73 GB/sec and 40.61 GB/sec respectively. Notably, single-threaded gzip compression demonstrated top-tier efficiency at 36.55 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded strong throughput of 15.22 GB/sec. For lightweight artificial intelligence tasks, the instance achieved a strong 271.19 tokens/sec during text generation on a 135M parameter LLM model, though medium 7B model generation normalized to an average 10.18 tokens/sec.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-memory configuration and lack of local storage, the D8s_v7 delivers steady qualitative resource density for non-storage-bound enterprise services. It is technically appropriate for running mid-tier relational databases, application servers, Redis in-memory caches, static web serving, and generalized CI/CD pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores via multithreading), 32.0 GB of RAM, and a 480 MB L3 cache, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include dedicated GPUs or local storage, necessitating external storage volumes. Benchmark metrics exhibit standard middle-tier performance across raw compute and memory bandwidth, alongside elevated results in single-threaded compression (36.55 GB/sec gzip throughput) and small LLM text generation (271.19 tokens/sec). Benefiting from Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction support, the D8s_v7 represents a predictable, cost-balanced resource profile for mid-tier enterprise software, web serving, in-memory caching, and general-purpose business applications.
